notes: Company: regional multi-hospital health system + specialty clinics (~28 sites). Heavy PHI in notes/EHR attachments.
Primary contact: Sarah Munro (Dir. Digital Health) - wants sub-150ms retrieval for chart summarization queries and <250ms end-to-end for clinician-facing search.

POC goals: 1) index 10-15M clinical notes + attachments metadata, 2) provide 99th perc latency <= 250ms (95th <= 120ms) on retrieval+rerank, 3) cost target <$0.08/query at avg QPS 5 with bursts to 150.
Architecture preference: VPC-private deployment in their AWS accounts or Redwood Private on prem for auditability. Willing to evaluate Dedicated with private peering if Private too heavy.

Security: must sign BAA; SOC2 + HIPAA proof required. KMS integration mandatory; customer-managed keys preferred. Full audit logs per patient access (per-request user + token) and 7-year retention for access logs.
Data residency: US primary, but some legacy datasets in EU — potential requirement to pin EU subsets to EU region. Must support network restrictions (no egress to public internet for data plane).

Embedding strategy discussed: hybrid index — dense embeddings for semantic recall + term-level inverted indices for fast filters. Interested in 8-bit quantized models to reduce storage/cost if quality preserved.
Reranking: prefer to do inexpensive candidate retrieval on GPU, then CPU-based cross-encoder rerank in Dedicated/Private to cut cost. Concern about latency for cross-encoders at scale.
Cost sensitivity: strong — finance models at ORT show they need per-query cost predictability; open to Redwood Optimize recommendations on batching + caching to hit targets.
Quotes: 'If we can't guarantee auditable access for every PHI hit, procurement will stop this.' — Sarah Munro on legal call 2026-01-19.
Procurement: expects a 60-90 day security & legal review. Procurement will require 3rd party pen test report and proof of customer KMS integration in POC.
POC dataset: sanitized subset available (100k notes) for initial run; full load timeline after BAA (target Q3 2026 to index 10M+ docs).
